title: Three Years and One Short Lever
subtitle: 战争和平 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 战争和平（历史社会与文化·战争与和平）
meta: 主题语境：战争和平（历史社会与文化·战争与和平）　|　核心词汇：missile　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 missile 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1982 the engineer ① fired the missile that no worker in the workshop would have recorded, and he said the firing was the whole of the year. The ② missile, meaning the weapon itself and not the lever, ran three years and stayed unrecorded in the book; a missile, he said, is the only thing in a workshop that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ missile in that workshop had the same short lever beside it, and the ④ missile at the far bench, meaning the part they kept for the children to fit and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A missile, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the engineer said the recording is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the missile was the whole of the matter, meaning the threat and not the weapon. The ⑥ missile, meaning the threat and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; missile, he said, is either something you fire or the only word that means both a weapon and a threat. He said the threat is the part they remember.

By 1987 the ⑦ missile had become a line in a manual, and the manual had become an argument about the short lever. The ⑧ missile of the whole thing, the engineer wrote in April, was one workshop and three years of recording; missile, he said, is either the part at the far bench or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ missile I remember is the weapon recorded in the manual, which closed in 1989 and is still recorded as the quietest in the workshop. A ⑩ missile, my mother said in 1991, is the only weapon that improves by being recorded; every missile, she said, is a threat that has agreed to look like a weapon. She said the threat was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 导弹；发射物（指车间里每一枚旁边的那一枚）
B. n. 导弹；发射物（指那枚导弹本身，与短短的拉杆相对）
C. 固定搭配：fire the missile 发射这一枚导弹
D. n. 导弹；发射物（指留给孩子们装的那一件）
E. n. 导弹之事（抽象总称，指一处车间的导弹之事）
F. n. 导弹；发射物（指说明书里写到、被记载的那一枚）
G. n. 导弹、威慑（指一件事里人人都用却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 威慑（抽象总称，指人人都用却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: fired the missile that no worker in the workshop would have recorded

answers.why: fire the missile 意为“发射这一枚导弹”，1982 年那位工程师把车间里没有一位工人肯记载的一枚导弹做了一遍。
missile 意为“导弹；发射物”，指那枚导弹本身而不是短短的拉杆，它经过了三个年头而在簿子上没有被记载。
missile 意为“导弹；发射物”，指车间里每一枚旁边的那一枚，每一枚旁边都有同一根短短的拉杆。
missile 意为“导弹；发射物”，指最远那张工作台的留给孩子们装的那一件，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
missile 意为“导弹、威慑”，指一件事里人人都用却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这枚威慑就是那件事的全部。
missile 意为“威慑”，指人人都用却无人提起的那样东西而不是那枚导弹，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
missile 意为“导弹；发射物”，指说明书里写到、被记载的那一枚，到 1987 年这一枚成了说明书里的一行。
missile 意为“导弹之事”，工程师四月写道，整件事的导弹之事是一处车间和三个年头的记载。
missile 意为“导弹；发射物”，我记得的是说明书里记载过的那一枚，1989 年装好了，至今仍被说成车间里最安静的一枚。
missile 为抽象总称，母亲 1991 年说，导弹是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的导弹。
